chapter: Reception in Germany and Berlin scene
title: Fundraising letters and Hübner's criticism of the Young Tuxedo Band
summary: Fundraising by letter had modest success; Dr. Hübner of Hamburg wrote that New Orleans birth does not guarantee good music, criticizing the Young Tuxedo recording.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Before you came here, did you find support? Did anyone interested you for? What was so on your heart? Or did the people have you for crazy?

Yes. Of course, I tried to do, because I originally wanted to take pictures, originally from musicians, who have been very few on plates until now. And there I had a round of writing, I spoke to all those people, from whom I believed that they were just interested in New Orleans Jazz. I also had a lot of success with that.

Yes, financial success. But of course, it was just a drop on a hot stone. And these people, they only came from the close friends. And all the people, musicians and so-called Jazz fans, who were always talking to them, they didn't have been called themselves, or they wrote me letters. And I also received some letters, from which I was very surprised and surprised. For example, I received a letter, and there was a letter, I said, I should have to let that be, and I should have to do it in Europe, in Germany, in Germany. There would be more than just in the United States than in the entire United States.

Yes, this letter I have just from one, that is the main speaker of the King Oliver direction in Germany. That is Dr. Abi Hübner from Hamburg, who wrote that. That is a very good trumpet. And his cell, they play in the Oliver direction. And there are also in Frankfurt, Oliver Benz, and this kind of, and also in Berlin. And they all belong to a company, which is called the Society for the New Orleans Jazz. And Mr. Hübner wrote, that he could not understand it, and that not only a birth certificate from New Orleans enough to make good music. And also this society that has a new Orleans Jazz, that has its main seat in Frankfurt, which was initially very excited for it, and that has then nothing more heard.
And what did you say about the Tuxedo Band? Oh, yes.

So, yes. He came then on the recording of the Young Tuxedo Band to talk and he said, King Oliver would have turned in the grave spiraling if he would have heard this ! Yeah, that is of course very sad, if we wanted to do that, and that we wanted to do that and that we would get such a brief and then get such a brief.
